q: Which AWS service is used to manage access to AWS resources using users, groups, roles, and policies?

exp.a: Incorrect. Cognito is for application user authentication, not AWS resource management.
exp.b: Correct. AWS IAM enables you to manage access to AWS services and resources using users, groups, roles, and policies.
exp.c: Incorrect. Organizations manages multiple AWS accounts.
exp.d: Incorrect. Directory Service provides managed Microsoft Active Directory.

q: What is the maximum number of IAM users you can create in a single AWS account?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 1,000.
exp.b: Correct. You can create a maximum of 5,000 IAM users per AWS account. For more users, use temporary credentials or IAM Identity Center.
exp.c: Incorrect. 10,000 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is a fixed limit of 5,000.

q: What is the maximum number of IAM groups per AWS account?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 100.
exp.b: Correct. You can create a maximum of 300 IAM groups per AWS account.
exp.c: Incorrect. 500 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 1,000 exceeds the limit.

q: What is the maximum number of IAM groups a single IAM user can belong to?

exp.a: Incorrect. A user can belong to more than 5 groups.
exp.b: Correct. A single IAM user can be a member of up to 10 IAM groups.
exp.c: Incorrect. 15 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 20 exceeds the limit.

q: What is the maximum number of managed policies that can be attached to an IAM user, group, or role?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 5.
exp.b: Correct. Up to 10 managed policies can be attached to a single IAM user, group, or role.
exp.c: Incorrect. 15 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 20 exceeds the limit.

q: What is the maximum number of access keys per IAM user?

exp.a: Incorrect. More than 1 access key is allowed.
exp.b: Correct. Each IAM user can have a maximum of 2 access keys, which facilitates key rotation.
exp.c: Incorrect. 3 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 5 exceeds the limit.

q: What is the maximum size of an IAM managed policy?

exp.a: Incorrect. 2,048 characters is the limit for inline policies on users.
exp.b: Correct. The maximum size of a managed policy is 6,144 characters (not including whitespace).
exp.c: Incorrect. 10,240 characters is the limit for role trust policies.
exp.d: Incorrect. 16,384 exceeds the limit.

q: Which AWS service provides DDoS protection at no additional cost for all AWS customers?

exp.a: Incorrect. WAF is a web application firewall with separate charges.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Shield Standard provides automatic protection against common DDoS attacks at no additional cost for all AWS customers.
exp.c: Incorrect. Shield Advanced costs $3,000/month.
exp.d: Incorrect. Firewall Manager has separate charges.

q: What is the monthly cost of AWS Shield Advanced?

exp.a: Incorrect. $1,000 is below the cost.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Shield Advanced costs $3,000 per month per organization (with a 1-year subscription commitment), plus data transfer fees.
exp.c: Incorrect. $5,000 exceeds the monthly cost.
exp.d: Incorrect. $10,000 exceeds the monthly cost.

q: What additional benefit does AWS Shield Advanced provide that Shield Standard does not?

opts.b: 24/7 access to AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT), cost protection, and advanced monitoring

exp.a: Incorrect. Basic DDoS protection is Shield Standard.
exp.b: Correct. Shield Advanced provides 24/7 DRT access, cost protection against scaling charges from DDoS attacks, advanced real-time monitoring, and WAF integration at no extra cost.
exp.c: Incorrect. SSL certificates are from ACM.
exp.d: Incorrect. Patching is not a Shield feature.

q: Which AWS service provides a web application firewall to protect against common web exploits?

exp.a: Incorrect. Shield is for DDoS protection.
exp.b: Correct. AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) protects web applications from common exploits like SQL injection, XSS, and other OWASP top 10 vulnerabilities.
exp.c: Incorrect. GuardDuty is a threat detection service.
exp.d: Incorrect. Network Firewall is for VPC-level network protection.

q: Which services can AWS WAF be deployed on?

opts.b: CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito, App Runner, and Verified Access

exp.a: Incorrect. WAF cannot be deployed directly on EC2.
exp.b: Correct. AWS WAF can be deployed on CloudFront, Application Load Balancer, API Gateway, AppSync, Amazon Cognito, App Runner, and AWS Verified Access.
exp.c: Incorrect. WAF is not deployed on S3.
exp.d: Incorrect. Route 53 and VPC are not WAF targets.

q: Which AWS service manages encryption keys and allows you to create, control, and rotate cryptographic keys?

exp.a: Incorrect. Secrets Manager stores secrets, not encryption keys.
exp.b: Correct. AWS KMS is a managed service for creating, managing, and controlling cryptographic keys used to encrypt data.
exp.c: Incorrect. ACM manages SSL/TLS certificates.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules.

q: What is the automatic rotation period for AWS KMS customer managed keys (symmetric)?

exp.a: Incorrect. 30 days is not the automatic rotation period.
exp.b: Incorrect. 90 days is not the automatic rotation period.
exp.c: Correct. When enabled, AWS KMS automatically rotates KMS keys every 365 days (1 year). You can also configure rotation between 90 and 2,560 days.
exp.d: Incorrect. 730 days is not the default rotation period.

q: What is the configurable range for KMS automatic key rotation?

exp.a: Incorrect. 30 days is below the minimum.
exp.b: Correct. As of 2024, KMS allows configuring automatic key rotation between 90 and 2,560 days (approximately 7 years).
exp.c: Incorrect. This is not the correct range.
exp.d: Incorrect. This is not the correct range.

q: What is the difference between AWS KMS and AWS CloudHSM?

opts.a: KMS is more expensive than CloudHSM
opts.b: KMS is a shared multi-tenant managed service; CloudHSM provides dedicated single-tenant hardware security modules

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudHSM is typically more expensive.
exp.b: Correct. KMS is a multi-tenant managed service, while CloudHSM provides dedicated FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated HSMs in your VPC for exclusive use.
exp.c: Incorrect. CloudHSM works with many services.
exp.d: Incorrect. KMS encrypts data across many AWS services.

q: What FIPS validation level does AWS CloudHSM meet?

exp.a: Incorrect. Level 1 is the lowest validation.
exp.b: Incorrect. Level 2 is not the correct level for CloudHSM.
exp.c: Correct. AWS CloudHSM uses FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security modules.
exp.d: Incorrect. Level 4 is the highest and not applicable to CloudHSM.

q: Which AWS service continuously monitors AWS accounts for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior using machine learning?

exp.a: Incorrect. Config evaluates resource compliance.
exp.b: Correct. Amazon GuardDuty is an intelligent threat detection service that continuously monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior using ML, anomaly detection, and integrated threat intelligence.
exp.c: Incorrect. CloudTrail logs API calls but doesn't detect threats.
exp.d: Incorrect. Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities.

q: What data sources does Amazon GuardDuty analyze?

opts.b: VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail Management Events, CloudTrail S3 Data Events, DNS Logs, EKS Audit Logs, RDS Login Activity, Lambda Network Activity, and Runtime Monitoring

exp.a: Incorrect. GuardDuty analyzes many more data sources.
exp.b: Correct. GuardDuty analyzes VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail events, DNS logs, EKS audit logs, RDS login activity, Lambda network activity, S3 data events, and runtime monitoring.
exp.c: Incorrect. CloudWatch metrics are not a GuardDuty source.
exp.d: Incorrect. GuardDuty uses multiple data sources.

q: How many days is the Amazon GuardDuty free trial?

exp.a: Incorrect. The free trial is longer than 7 days.
exp.b: Incorrect. The free trial is longer than 14 days.
exp.c: Correct. Amazon GuardDuty offers a 30-day free trial for new accounts.
exp.d: Incorrect. 90 days exceeds the free trial period.

q: Which AWS service scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure?

exp.a: Incorrect. GuardDuty detects threats, not vulnerabilities.
exp.b: Correct. Amazon Inspector automatically scans EC2 instances, container images in ECR, and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.
exp.c: Incorrect. Security Hub aggregates findings.
exp.d: Incorrect. Macie discovers sensitive data.

q: Which AWS service discovers and protects sensitive data stored in Amazon S3?

exp.a: Incorrect. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.
exp.b: Correct. Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover, classify, and protect sensitive data (like PII, financial data) in S3.
exp.c: Incorrect. Config checks resource compliance.
exp.d: Incorrect. GuardDuty detects threats.

q: Which AWS service provides a comprehensive view of security alerts and compliance status across AWS accounts?

exp.a: Incorrect. GuardDuty is a threat detection service.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Security Hub aggregates, organizes, and prioritizes security findings from multiple AWS services (GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, etc.) and third-party tools into a single dashboard.
exp.c: Incorrect. CloudTrail logs API activity.
exp.d: Incorrect. Detective investigates security findings.

q: What finding format does AWS Security Hub use?

exp.a: Incorrect. JWT is for authentication tokens.
exp.b: Correct. Security Hub uses the AWS Security Finding Format (ASFF), a standardized format for all security findings.
exp.c: Incorrect. CEF is used by SIEM tools.
exp.d: Incorrect. STIX/TAXII is for threat intelligence sharing.

q: Which AWS service records all API calls made in your AWS account?

exp.a: Incorrect. Config tracks resource configuration changes.
exp.b: Correct. AWS CloudTrail records API calls and events for your AWS account, providing governance, compliance, and auditing capabilities.
exp.c: Incorrect. CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs.
exp.d: Incorrect. Security Hub aggregates security findings.

q: How many days of event history does AWS CloudTrail retain by default (without creating a trail)?

exp.a: Incorrect. Default retention is longer than 30 days.
exp.b: Incorrect. Default retention is longer than 60 days.
exp.c: Correct. CloudTrail retains 90 days of management event history by default in the Event History. For longer retention, create a trail to deliver events to S3.
exp.d: Incorrect. 365 days requires a configured trail.

q: What are the two types of events that CloudTrail can log?

exp.a: Incorrect. Read/Write are subcategories, not the main types.
exp.b: Correct. CloudTrail logs Management events (control plane operations like creating/deleting resources) and Data events (data plane operations like S3 object-level operations, Lambda invocations).
exp.c: Incorrect. These are not the official CloudTrail event types.
exp.d: Incorrect. These are not CloudTrail categories.

q: Which AWS service continuously evaluates AWS resource configurations for compliance?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudTrail records API calls.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Config continuously monitors and records AWS resource configurations and evaluates them against desired configurations using Config rules.
exp.c: Incorrect. Audit Manager automates evidence collection for audits.
exp.d: Incorrect. Trusted Advisor provides best practice recommendations.

q: Which AWS service stores and automatically rotates database credentials, API keys, and other secrets?

exp.a: Incorrect. KMS manages encryption keys, not secrets.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Secrets Manager stores, retrieves, and automatically rotates secrets like database credentials, API keys, and OAuth tokens.
exp.c: Incorrect. Parameter Store can store secrets but lacks native automatic rotation.
exp.d: Incorrect. ACM manages SSL/TLS certificates.

q: What minimum rotation period can you configure for AWS Secrets Manager?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 hour is below the minimum.
exp.b: Incorrect. 1 day is longer than the minimum.
exp.c: Correct. AWS Secrets Manager supports automatic rotation with a minimum period of 4 hours and maximum of 365 days.
exp.d: Incorrect. 7 days is longer than the minimum.

q: A company wants to detect when secret values are changed in Secrets Manager and automatically refresh application caches. What 2026 feature enables this without complex CloudTrail parsing?

opts.b: Secrets Manager native EventBridge events for secret value changes

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudWatch integration is not the correct mechanism.
exp.b: Correct. As of July 2026, Secrets Manager automatically publishes events to EventBridge whenever secret values change, eliminating the need for complex CloudTrail parsing.
exp.c: Incorrect. Direct SNS notifications were not the new feature.
exp.d: Incorrect. Lambda triggers are not the native mechanism.

q: Which AWS service provides free public SSL/TLS certificates?

exp.a: Incorrect. KMS is for encryption keys.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provides free public SSL/TLS certificates and handles automatic renewal for certificates used with AWS services like CloudFront and ALB.
exp.c: Incorrect. CloudHSM is for hardware security modules.
exp.d: Incorrect. Secrets Manager stores secrets.

q: What is the validity period of a public certificate issued by AWS Certificate Manager?

exp.a: Incorrect. 90 days is too short for ACM public certificates.
exp.b: Incorrect. While close, 395 days is not exact.
exp.c: Correct. ACM public certificates are valid for 13 months (395 days) and are automatically renewed before expiration.
exp.d: Incorrect. 2 years exceeds the validity period.

q: Which AWS service helps investigate security findings by analyzing and visualizing data from multiple sources?

exp.a: Incorrect. GuardDuty detects threats but doesn't investigate them.
exp.b: Correct. Amazon Detective makes it easy to analyze, investigate, and identify the root cause of potential security issues using graph analysis and machine learning.
exp.c: Incorrect. Security Hub aggregates findings but doesn't investigate.
exp.d: Incorrect. Macie discovers sensitive data.

q: Which AWS service provides access to AWS compliance reports and agreements (like SOC, PCI, ISO)?

exp.a: Incorrect. Audit Manager automates evidence collection.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS security and compliance reports and select online agreements.
exp.c: Incorrect. Config evaluates resource configurations.
exp.d: Incorrect. Security Hub shows security posture.

q: Which AWS service provides centralized management of firewall rules across accounts and resources?

exp.a: Incorrect. WAF alone doesn't provide centralized multi-account management.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Firewall Manager centrally configures and manages firewall rules across accounts and applications in AWS Organizations (WAF, Shield Advanced, Security Groups, Network Firewall, Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall).
exp.c: Incorrect. Network Firewall protects VPCs but isn't for centralized management.
exp.d: Incorrect. Security Groups are per-instance firewalls.

q: Which AWS service provides stateful network-level firewall protection for VPCs?

exp.a: Incorrect. WAF operates at the application layer (Layer 7).
exp.b: Correct. AWS Network Firewall is a managed service that provides stateful inspection, intrusion prevention, and web filtering for VPC traffic.
exp.c: Incorrect. Security Groups are stateful but limited in inspection capabilities.
exp.d: Incorrect. NACLs are stateless and operate at subnet level.

q: A company needs to protect a web application from SQL injection and XSS attacks. Which AWS service should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. Shield protects against DDoS, not application-layer attacks.
exp.b: Correct. AWS WAF protects against common web exploits including SQL injection and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) through configurable rules.
exp.c: Incorrect. Network Firewall is for network-level protection.
exp.d: Incorrect. GuardDuty detects threats but doesn't block them.

q: A company wants to enforce that no S3 bucket can ever be made public across all accounts in their organization. Which feature should they use?

opts.b: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations

exp.a: Incorrect. IAM policies per account don't provide organization-wide enforcement.
exp.b: Correct. SCPs in AWS Organizations provide guardrails that restrict what actions are allowed across all accounts, even for root users in member accounts.
exp.c: Incorrect. Config rules detect but don't prevent.
exp.d: Incorrect. Bucket policies are per-bucket and can be changed.

q: What is the successor to AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO)?

exp.a: Incorrect. Cognito is for application user management.
exp.b: Correct. AWS IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO) provides centralized access management for multiple AWS accounts and business applications.
exp.c: Incorrect. Directory Service provides managed AD.
exp.d: Incorrect. AWS Federation is a concept, not a specific service.

q: Which AWS service provides fine-grained authorization for custom applications using Cedar policy language?

exp.a: Incorrect. IAM is for AWS resource access.
exp.b: Correct. Amazon Verified Permissions is a fine-grained permissions management service that uses the Cedar policy language for custom application authorization.
exp.c: Incorrect. Cognito handles authentication.
exp.d: Incorrect. Identity Center is for AWS account access.

q: Which service centralizes security data from AWS and partner sources into a unified data lake?

exp.a: Incorrect. Security Hub aggregates findings, not raw data.
exp.b: Correct. Amazon Security Lake automatically centralizes security data from AWS, partners, and custom sources into a purpose-built data lake using the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF).
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 is generic storage, not a security-specific data lake.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudTrail Lake is specifically for CloudTrail data.

q: What open standard does Amazon Security Lake use for data normalization?

exp.a: Incorrect. STIX/TAXII is for threat intelligence sharing.
exp.b: Correct. Amazon Security Lake normalizes and combines security data into the OCSF standard, making it easier to analyze across multiple sources.
exp.c: Incorrect. CEF is a SIEM format.
exp.d: Incorrect. ASFF is Security Hub's format.

q: Which IAM feature analyzes access activity to identify unused permissions and external access?

exp.a: Incorrect. Policy Simulator tests policy effects.
exp.b: Correct. IAM Access Analyzer identifies resources shared externally, validates policies, and generates least-privilege policies based on access activity.
exp.c: Incorrect. Credentials Report lists user credential status.
exp.d: Incorrect. Access Advisor shows service last-accessed data.

q: A security team needs to identify all S3 buckets and IAM roles shared with external accounts. Which service should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. Macie finds sensitive data, not external sharing.
exp.b: Correct. IAM Access Analyzer identifies resources (S3 buckets, IAM roles, KMS keys, Lambda functions, SQS queues) that are shared with external entities.
exp.c: Incorrect. Config checks compliance, not external sharing specifically.
exp.d: Incorrect. GuardDuty detects threats.

q: What type of MFA device provides the highest level of security for AWS accounts according to AWS?

exp.a: Incorrect. Virtual MFA is good but not the highest security.
exp.b: Correct. FIDO2 security keys (like YubiKey) provide the strongest phishing-resistant MFA. AWS supports FIDO2/WebAuthn as MFA and passkeys.
exp.c: Incorrect. SMS is not supported as MFA for IAM users.
exp.d: Incorrect. Email verification is not MFA.

q: How many MFA devices can be assigned to a single IAM user?

exp.a: Incorrect. More than 1 MFA device can be assigned.
exp.b: Incorrect. More than 2 can be assigned.
exp.c: Incorrect. More than 5 can be assigned.
exp.d: Correct. Up to 8 MFA devices can be assigned to a single IAM user, including any combination of virtual MFA and FIDO2 security keys.

q: What is the recommended best practice for the AWS root account?

opts.b: Enable MFA, do not use for daily tasks, and lock away access keys
opts.c: Share it with the team lead
opts.d: Delete it after creating IAM users

exp.a: Incorrect. Root should not be used for daily operations.
exp.b: Correct. AWS recommends enabling MFA on root, not using it for everyday tasks, not creating access keys for root, and using IAM users/roles instead.
exp.c: Incorrect. Root credentials should never be shared.
exp.d: Incorrect. Root cannot be deleted.

q: Which encryption type in AWS means that AWS manages the encryption/decryption process transparently?

exp.a: Incorrect. Client-side means you encrypt before sending to AWS.
exp.b: Correct. Server-side encryption means AWS encrypts data after receiving it and decrypts when you access it. Services like S3, EBS, and RDS support this.
exp.c: Incorrect. End-to-end is not a specific AWS encryption classification.
exp.d: Incorrect. Application-level is not AWS's terminology.

q: What are the three types of KMS keys?

opts.b: AWS owned keys, AWS managed keys, Customer managed keys

exp.a: Incorrect. These are not KMS key categories.
exp.b: Correct. KMS has three categories: AWS owned keys (free, shared, no visibility), AWS managed keys (free, per-service like aws/s3), and Customer managed keys ($1/month + API charges).
exp.c: Incorrect. Symmetric/Asymmetric describes key type, not ownership.
exp.d: Incorrect. These are not KMS categories.

q: What is the monthly cost of a Customer Managed Key (CMK) in AWS KMS?

exp.a: Incorrect. Customer managed keys are not free (AWS managed keys are free).
exp.b: Correct. Customer managed KMS keys cost $1 per month per key, plus $0.03 per 10,000 API requests.
exp.c: Incorrect. $5 exceeds the cost.
exp.d: Incorrect. $10 exceeds the cost.

q: A company needs to encrypt data at rest in S3 and wants AWS to manage the encryption keys with no cost. Which option should they choose?

exp.a: Incorrect. SSE-C requires you to provide and manage keys.
exp.b: Correct. SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys at no additional cost. It's the default encryption for S3 as of January 2023.
exp.c: Incorrect. CMK costs $1/month per key.
exp.d: Incorrect. Client-side encryption requires you to manage everything.

q: Since January 2023, what is the default encryption for all new S3 objects?

exp.a: Incorrect. All new objects are encrypted by default since January 2023.
exp.b: Correct. Since January 5, 2023, Amazon S3 automatically encrypts all new objects with SSE-S3 (AES-256) at no additional cost.
exp.c: Incorrect. SSE-KMS is available but not the default.
exp.d: Incorrect. SSE-C is not the default.

q: A company needs to ensure all EC2 instances are launched only in specific Regions across their organization. Which service should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. IAM policies don't provide organization-wide guardrails.
exp.b: Correct. SCPs in AWS Organizations can restrict which Regions resources can be created in, applying across all accounts in the organization.
exp.c: Incorrect. Config detects but doesn't prevent.
exp.d: Incorrect. Security Groups are for network access.

q: Which AWS service automates evidence collection for audits?

exp.a: Incorrect. Artifact provides compliance reports.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Audit Manager continuously audits your AWS usage to simplify risk and compliance assessment, automating evidence collection.
exp.c: Incorrect. Config evaluates resource compliance.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudTrail records API calls.

q: What is the difference between Security Groups and NACLs?

opts.a: Security Groups are stateless; NACLs are stateful
opts.b: Security Groups are stateful (instance level); NACLs are stateless (subnet level)

exp.a: Incorrect. This is reversed.
exp.b: Correct. Security Groups are stateful (return traffic automatically allowed) and operate at instance level. NACLs are stateless (must explicitly allow return traffic) and operate at subnet level.
exp.c: Incorrect. NACLs are stateless.
exp.d: Incorrect. Security Groups are stateful.

q: What is the default number of rules allowed in a Security Group (inbound + outbound)?

exp.a: Incorrect. 50 is below the default.
exp.b: Correct. By default, a security group can have up to 60 inbound rules and 60 outbound rules.
exp.c: Incorrect. 100 exceeds the default.
exp.d: Incorrect. 200 exceeds the default.

q: What is the default number of security groups that can be associated with a network interface?

exp.a: Incorrect. More than 3 can be associated.
exp.b: Correct. By default, up to 5 security groups can be associated with a single network interface.
exp.c: Incorrect. 10 exceeds the default.
exp.d: Incorrect. 15 exceeds the default.

q: What is the default maximum number of NACLs per VPC?

exp.a: Incorrect. The default is higher.
exp.b: Correct. The default quota is 200 NACLs per VPC.
exp.c: Incorrect. 300 exceeds the default.
exp.d: Incorrect. 500 exceeds the default.

q: What is the maximum number of rules per NACL?

exp.a: Incorrect. 10 is below the limit.
exp.b: Correct. Each NACL can have up to 20 inbound rules and 20 outbound rules by default.
exp.c: Incorrect. 40 exceeds the default per direction.
exp.d: Incorrect. 100 exceeds the limit.

q: A developer accidentally committed AWS access keys to a public GitHub repository. Which AWS service would detect this?

exp.a: Incorrect. Config doesn't scan GitHub.
exp.b: Incorrect. GuardDuty might detect unusual API activity from the compromised key.
exp.c: Incorrect. Access Analyzer checks resource sharing, not GitHub.
exp.d: Correct. AWS actively scans public repositories and sends notifications through AWS Health if exposed keys are found, and may restrict the keys.

q: What does the IAM policy evaluation logic default to when there's no explicit Allow or Deny?

exp.a: Incorrect. The default is not Allow.
exp.b: Correct. In IAM, everything is implicitly denied by default. You must explicitly Allow access. An explicit Deny always overrides any Allow.
exp.c: Incorrect. The logic is consistent across services.
exp.d: Incorrect. There are no user prompts.

q: In IAM policy evaluation, what takes precedence?

opts.b: Explicit Deny always wins over Allow
opts.d: The policy attached to the group wins

exp.a: Incorrect. Deny overrides Allow.
exp.b: Correct. An explicit Deny in any policy always overrides any Allow. The evaluation order is: Explicit Deny > Explicit Allow > Implicit Deny.
exp.c: Incorrect. Recency doesn't determine precedence.
exp.d: Incorrect. Group policies don't automatically take precedence.

q: Which AWS service provides private certificate authority capabilities?

opts.b: AWS Private CA (formerly ACM Private CA)

exp.a: Incorrect. ACM provides public certificates and integrates with Private CA.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Private CA allows you to create private certificate authorities for issuing private certificates for internal resources.
exp.c: Incorrect. KMS manages encryption keys.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudHSM is for hardware key storage.

q: What is the cost per month for a general-purpose AWS Private CA?

exp.a: Incorrect. $50 is for short-lived certificate mode.
exp.b: Incorrect. $200 is not the correct cost.
exp.c: Correct. A general-purpose AWS Private CA costs $400 per month. Short-lived certificate mode costs $50 per month.
exp.d: Incorrect. $1,000 exceeds the cost.

q: A company needs to meet PCI-DSS compliance and wants to download AWS's compliance attestation. Which service should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. Security Hub shows security posture, not compliance reports.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports including PCI-DSS, SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001, and more.
exp.c: Incorrect. Audit Manager helps with your own compliance, not downloading AWS reports.
exp.d: Incorrect. Config checks resource compliance.

q: A company wants to block all traffic from specific countries to their web application hosted on CloudFront + ALB. Which service should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. Security Groups can't filter by country.
exp.b: Correct. AWS WAF supports geographic match (geo-match) conditions that allow blocking or allowing traffic based on country of origin.
exp.c: Incorrect. Shield is for DDoS protection, not geo-blocking.
exp.d: Incorrect. NACLs work with IP addresses, not countries directly.

q: What is the maximum number of Web ACLs you can create per Region per account in AWS WAF?

exp.a: Incorrect. 50 is below the default.
exp.b: Correct. The default quota is 100 Web ACLs per Region per account in AWS WAF.
exp.c: Incorrect. 500 exceeds the default.
exp.d: Incorrect. 1,000 exceeds the default.

q: What is the maximum number of rules per Web ACL in AWS WAF?

exp.a: Incorrect. 100 WCU is too low.
exp.b: Incorrect. 500 WCU is below the limit.
exp.c: Incorrect. 1,500 WCU is the default but can be increased.
exp.d: Correct. The maximum Web ACL capacity is 5,000 WCU per Web ACL (the default is 1,500 WCU, which can be increased).

q: Which AWS service provides DNS-level filtering to block domains associated with malware?

exp.a: Incorrect. WAF operates at the HTTP layer.
exp.b: Correct. Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall allows you to filter and regulate outbound DNS traffic from your VPC, blocking queries to known malicious domains.
exp.c: Incorrect. Network Firewall operates at the network level.
exp.d: Incorrect. GuardDuty detects DNS-based threats but doesn't block them.

q: What is AWS CloudTrail Lake?

opts.a: A storage service for CloudTrail logs in S3
opts.b: A managed data lake for auditing that lets you run SQL-based queries on CloudTrail events

exp.a: Incorrect. S3 delivery is a separate feature from CloudTrail Lake.
exp.b: Correct. CloudTrail Lake is a managed data lake that lets you run SQL-based queries on your CloudTrail events for auditing, security investigation, and troubleshooting.
exp.c: Incorrect. It's not a monitoring dashboard.
exp.d: Incorrect. It's for querying events, not generating compliance reports.

q: What is the maximum retention period for CloudTrail Lake event data stores?

exp.a: Incorrect. Retention can be longer than 1 year.
exp.b: Incorrect. Retention can be longer than 3 years.
exp.c: Correct. CloudTrail Lake event data stores can retain data for up to 2,557 days (approximately 7 years).
exp.d: Incorrect. 10 years exceeds the maximum.

q: Which AWS service should be used to share resources securely across AWS accounts without using resource-based policies?

exp.a: Incorrect. Organizations manages accounts but doesn't share resources.
exp.b: Correct. AWS RAM allows you to securely share AWS resources (subnets, Transit Gateways, Route 53 zones, etc.) across accounts and within your organization.
exp.c: Incorrect. Cross-account roles provide access, not resource sharing.
exp.d: Incorrect. PrivateLink provides private connectivity to services.

q: A company discovered unauthorized API calls in their account. They need to investigate who made the calls, from where, and when. Which services should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. Config and Macie don't help with API call investigation.
exp.b: Correct. CloudTrail provides the audit trail of API calls (who, what, when, where), and Detective helps analyze and visualize the investigation.
exp.c: Incorrect. WAF and Shield are for web and DDoS protection.
exp.d: Incorrect. Inspector is for vulnerability scanning.

q: A security team needs to ensure all EBS volumes across the organization are encrypted. Which service provides continuous monitoring and alerting for non-compliance?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudTrail logs calls but doesn't evaluate compliance.
exp.b: Correct. AWS Config with the 'encrypted-volumes' managed rule continuously checks if EBS volumes are encrypted and alerts on non-compliant resources.
exp.c: Incorrect. Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, not encryption compliance.
exp.d: Incorrect. Artifact provides compliance reports.

q: What does the principle of least privilege mean in AWS IAM?

opts.b: Grant only the permissions required to perform a specific task
opts.c: Create one policy for all users
opts.d: Allow all actions and deny specific ones

exp.a: Incorrect. Admin access violates least privilege.
exp.b: Correct. Least privilege means granting only the minimum permissions necessary for a user, role, or service to perform their required task — nothing more.
exp.c: Incorrect. One policy for all doesn't provide minimal access.
exp.d: Incorrect. The correct approach is to deny all and allow only what's needed.

q: What IAM feature helps you generate least-privilege policies based on actual access activity?

exp.a: Incorrect. Policy Simulator tests existing policies.
exp.b: Correct. IAM Access Analyzer can generate IAM policies based on access activity captured in CloudTrail logs, helping create least-privilege policies.
exp.c: Incorrect. Credentials Report shows user status.
exp.d: Incorrect. Access Advisor shows which services were used but doesn't generate policies.

q: What does 'encryption in transit' mean in AWS?

opts.b: Encrypting data as it moves between endpoints (e.g., using TLS/SSL)

exp.a: Incorrect. That's encryption at rest.
exp.b: Correct. Encryption in transit protects data as it moves between systems, typically using TLS/SSL protocols (HTTPS, TLS connections to databases, etc.).
exp.c: Incorrect. Backup encryption is encryption at rest.
exp.d: Incorrect. Log encryption is encryption at rest.

q: Which AWS service provides managed threat intelligence feeds integrated with other security services?

exp.a: Correct. Amazon GuardDuty uses integrated threat intelligence from AWS, CrowdStrike, and Proofpoint to detect known malicious IPs, domains, and behaviors.
exp.b: Incorrect. Security Hub aggregates findings but doesn't provide threat intelligence.
exp.c: Incorrect. Detective investigates findings.
exp.d: Incorrect. Trusted Advisor provides best practice recommendations.

q: What is the maximum number of IAM roles per AWS account?

exp.a: Incorrect. 500 is below the limit.
exp.b: Correct. The default maximum number of IAM roles per AWS account is 1,000 (this is a soft limit that can be increased).
exp.c: Incorrect. 5,000 is the user limit, not roles.
exp.d: Incorrect. 10,000 exceeds the default.

q: What is the maximum session duration for an IAM role when assumed?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 hour is the default but not the maximum.
exp.b: Incorrect. 4 hours is below the maximum.
exp.c: Correct. IAM roles can have a maximum session duration of 12 hours (configurable from 1 hour to 12 hours).
exp.d: Incorrect. 36 hours exceeds the maximum.
